claude-code.notes: Skills live in .claude/skills/ (project) and ~/.claude/skills/ (personal); sub-agents in .claude/agents/ (project) or ~/.claude/agents/. The primary session is the orchestrator and dispatches sub-agents; do not design a separate orchestrator agent. Scheduled tasks and auto memory exist here; do not assume auto memory exists in Claude on the web or desktop (Claude has its own scheduled tasks — see the `claude` entry).

capabilities.skill_install: Skills are folders under .claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md in the project folder (or ~/.claude/skills/ for personal ones); Claude Code loads them when a chat is opened in that folder. To start one in a new chat, open a new Claude Code session in the same folder and type /<skill-name> (or ask for it by name). Nothing to upload or install. Verified 2026-09-29: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
capabilities.context_location: The project folder is the workspace: every chat opened in that folder reads and writes the same files (registry/, framework/, outputs/, .claude/), so a results file written in one chat is visible in the next. Files a workflow needs go in the project folder and are referenced by relative path. Verified 2026-09-29: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
capabilities.unattended_runs: Three options. Cloud routines run on a schedule without the machine on, from a fresh clone of the repo with connectors configured per task — no access to local files, so context must be in the repo or a connected source. Desktop scheduled tasks run on the user's machine (must be on) and can reach local files and configured MCP servers. In-session /loop tasks run only while a session is open and expire after seven days — not for production. Verified 2026-10-08: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks

claude.notes: Claude — on the web, on desktop, and on mobile. Chat and Cowork are one app now: older Design Specs that say Cowork, Claude.ai, or Claude Chat mean this entry, and are built the same way. Claude creates skills itself and saves them to the user's account; skills and sub-agents use Claude Code markdown formats. Skill and agent directories are system-managed: a standalone skill is saved through the Save skill flow (zip package), and plugins install from Customize > Plugins, either by uploading a plugin .zip directly (Add plugin > Upload plugin; no GitHub needed) or from a marketplace on a GitHub repo (plugin zip upload owner-verified 2026-10-18). Plugin skills, hooks, and sub-agents run on the web and on desktop; custom sub-agents run only when packaged inside an installed plugin, so a workflow with worker agents must package as Plugin. The one split: only the desktop app works on files and folders on the user's computer. No verified user-facing memory feature like Claude Code auto-memory — do not assume it exists here. Sources (verified 2026-09-22; Chat/Cowork merge, web sub-agents, and web scheduling owner-verified 2026-10-11): https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork, https://claude.com/blog/web-search, https://claude.com/docs/cowork/3p/extensions, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects. Operational note (inferred, not from the articles): authorize every connector the workflow touches in the account that runs a scheduled task before its first run.

capabilities.skill_install: Claude creates the skill and saves it to the user's account (the Save skill flow, a zip package); a plugin — required whenever the workflow has worker agents — installs from Customize > Plugins by uploading the plugin .zip (Add plugin > Upload plugin), or from a GitHub marketplace when the team shares one. Skill and agent directories are system-managed: on the desktop app, stage the source files in the working folder; on the web, Claude produces the package in the chat. Start it in a new chat by asking for the skill by name (Claude applies a matching skill automatically); with the plugin installed, typing `/` lists the available skills.
capabilities.context_location: On the desktop app, context files live in the working folder Claude is pointed at, and the skill references them by relative path; every chat opened on that folder reads and writes the same files (registry/, framework/, outputs/), so a file written in one chat is visible in the next. On the web, a Claude Project's knowledge holds the context files; start a fresh chat inside the project to run the workflow with them. Small reference material can ship inside the skill package on either.
capabilities.custom_agents: Yes — as worker sub-agents packaged in an installed plugin (agents/ directory, Claude Code markdown format), on the web and on desktop. The main Claude session is the orchestrator and dispatches them; do not design a separate orchestrator agent.
capabilities.unattended_runs: Scheduled tasks run on the web and on desktop, on their chosen cadence, even when the desktop app is closed or the computer is asleep, using the connectors, skills, and plugins set up in the account. A task that needs local files or apps runs only on the desktop app while it is open — so a workflow whose context lives in a local working folder cannot run on a remote schedule unless that context ships inside the skill package or a connected cloud source.
capabilities.web_search: Available, standard on all plans including free.

openai-codex.notes: Codex CLI, the Codex tab of the ChatGPT desktop app, and the IDE extension. Skills are folders read from $CWD/.agents/skills up to the repo root, then ~/.agents/skills (user-level default), then /etc/codex/skills; invoke with $skill-name or /skills. Plugins install from a marketplace (Plugins > Add marketplace in the app, or `codex plugin marketplace add owner/repo` in the CLI); ChatGPT and Codex share one plugin directory.

capabilities.skill_install: Skills are folders read from $CWD/.agents/skills up to the repo root, then ~/.agents/skills; start one in a new Codex session opened in the same folder with $skill-name or /skills. Best-effort — not verified this release.
capabilities.context_location: The working folder is the workspace; every session opened in it reads and writes the same files, so a results file written in one session is visible in the next. Best-effort — not verified this release.

gemini-cli.notes: Skills are folders under .gemini/skills/ (project) or ~/.gemini/skills/ (personal), each with a SKILL.md; invoke by name in the CLI.

capabilities.skill_install: Skills are folders under .gemini/skills/<skill-name>/ (project) or ~/.gemini/skills/ (personal), each with a SKILL.md; start one in a new Gemini CLI session opened in the same folder by asking for it by name. Best-effort — not verified this release.
capabilities.context_location: The working folder is the workspace; every session opened in it reads and writes the same files. Best-effort — not verified this release.

gemini-enterprise.notes: Work/school Google accounts on Standard, Plus, or Pay-as-you-go editions. Skills upload as Markdown or a zip with SKILL.md in the root directory via Skills > + > Upload skill > Import; invoke with @ or /. Skills are not available inside Gemini Enterprise agents. Personal Google accounts use Gemini Spark instead (see gemini-spark).

capabilities.skill_install: Best-effort — not verified this release: Skills upload as Markdown or a zip with SKILL.md in the root directory via Skills > + > Upload skill > Import; invoke with @ or / in a new chat.
capabilities.context_location: Best-effort — not verified this release: no dedicated project/context-file location is documented for this entry; treat any workflow context as shipped inside the skill package until this is verified.
capabilities.custom_agents: Best-effort — not verified this release: yes, via Agent Designer — but uploaded skills are not available inside Gemini Enterprise agents, so agent-shaped work and skill-shaped work do not compose on this platform today.
capabilities.unattended_runs: Best-effort — not verified this release: no scheduled or unattended run mechanism is documented for this entry.
capabilities.web_search: Best-effort — not verified this release: web search is available.

gemini-spark.notes: Spark is a mode of the Gemini app (sidebar > Switch to Spark) on the web, the Mac app, and Android/iOS. Personal Google accounts only (not Workspace), Google AI Pro or Ultra, 18+; not available in the EEA, UK, Switzerland, or Nigeria. Skills upload as a SKILL.md or a zip containing one via Skills > Upload; invoke with / in a task or let Spark pick automatically. Skill names must be lowercase-hyphenated.

capabilities.skill_install: Best-effort — not verified this release: Skills upload as a SKILL.md or a zip containing one via Skills > Upload; invoke with / in a new task or let Spark pick automatically.
capabilities.context_location: Best-effort — not verified this release: no dedicated project/context-file location is documented for this entry; treat any workflow context as shipped inside the skill package until this is verified.
capabilities.custom_agents: Best-effort — not verified this release: no custom-agent primitive is documented for Spark.
capabilities.unattended_runs: Best-effort — not verified this release: no scheduled or unattended run mechanism is documented for this entry.
capabilities.web_search: Best-effort — not verified this release: web search is available.

chatgpt.notes: ChatGPT Chat/Work on web, desktop, and mobile. Skills upload as a zip or SKILL.md under Plugins > Skills > Create > Upload from your computer (paid plans except Free/Go; off by default on Enterprise/Edu until an admin enables); invoke with @skill-name in Work. Plugins (any paid plan) install from Plugins > Add marketplace; plugin-bundled skills work across web, desktop, and mobile. Custom GPTs are deprecated — package agent-shaped work as a Workspace Agent with skills attached. Verified 2026-09-22: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001143-chatgpt-workspace-agents-for-enterprise-and-business, https://openai.com/index/introducing-workspace-agents-in-chatgpt/, https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10291617-scheduled-tasks-in-chatgpt, https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-chatgpt-search (help.openai.com/en/articles/20001066-skills-in-chatgpt returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; corroborated via openai.com/academy/skills and developers.openai.com/codex/skills-and-plugins for the @skill-name invocation).

capabilities.skill_install: Upload the skill as a zip or SKILL.md under Plugins > Skills > Create > Upload from your computer (paid plans except Free/Go; off by default on Enterprise/Edu until an admin enables). Invoke with @skill-name in a new chat, or let ChatGPT auto-match it to the task.
capabilities.context_location: Project files in a ChatGPT Project hold the workflow's context; run the workflow in a new chat inside that project. Small reference material ships inside the skill zip.
capabilities.custom_agents: Workspace Agents are the agent primitive (Custom GPTs are deprecated): build one from Agents > Browse templates or Agents > Create with the Agent Builder, then connect tools and skills to it. In research preview for Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Teachers plans as of this verification.
capabilities.unattended_runs: Scheduled tasks exist on every plan including Free, as one-time or recurring reminders up to once a day. Event-triggered tasks tied to a connected Gmail, Slack, or GitHub account are further limited to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare workspaces (not Free/Go), and can access only the connected account and its existing app permissions — connector authorization must be completed before the first such run.
capabilities.web_search: Available on Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans, including for signed-out users; triggered automatically or manually via the Search tool, subject to plan usage limits.

integration-registries.name: platform-native-connectors
integration-registries.notes: First stop: the platform entry's capabilities. Claude and ChatGPT ship native connectors for common tools; recommend those before any MCP server, API, or CLI.
